title: Fed Just Paused, But Prediction Markets Aren't Buying It—Polymarket Sees 82% December Hike Odds
detail:
Fed Just Paused, But Prediction Markets Aren't Buying It—Polymarket Sees 82% December Hike Odds
Fed Holds Rates, but Two Officials Push for Hike as Polymarket December Odds Hit 82%

The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady Wednesday, but two policymakers voted for another hike, highlighting concern over persistent inflation.

The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10–2 to maintain rates at 3.75%–4.00%, with Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack both favoring a quarter-point increase.

It was Cook's first dissent since joining the Fed in 2022, coming as President Donald Trump has repeatedly sought to remove her from office.

The Fed's statement described economic activity as expanding strongly, with resilient domestic spending and robust investment, despite continued geopolitical uncertainty.

"Inflation remains elevated," the committee said.

Polymarket Sees December Hike Odds Climb

On Polymarket, traders now assign an 82% probability to a 25-basis-point increase in December, up from roughly 77% before Wednesday's announcement.

The market has attracted more than $5.3 million in trading volume, with traders focused on whether Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will signal another increase before year-end.

Jesse Marre, senior portfolio manager at Hilbert Group, had expected the Fed to hold off until December rather than surprise markets with an immediate hike.

"I would be very surprised if the Fed shocked the market with a hike that is neither immediately required nor urgent when it can go in December instead," Marre said ahead of the announcement.

Inflation Pressures Persist Despite Weak Hiring.

Despite September's weak jobs report, which showed employers added just 29,000 positions, the Fed said job gains have kept pace with the workforce and unemployment has changed little.

Inflation-data provider Truflation forecasts September's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation at 3.6% annually, up from 3.4% in August.

Its estimates show gasoline and other energy goods rising 33.7% year over year, amid surging oil prices and supply disruptions linked to the Iran war.

Last week's rising crude prices helped push the Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSE:XLE) to a record high.

If oil remains elevated, it could strengthen the case for another rate hike in December, even with hiring weak.

The official PCE report arrives Thursday at 8:30 a.m. ET, alongside third-quarter GDP figures. Hotter-than-expected inflation or stronger economic growth could reinforce bets on a December hike, while softer data may ease pressure on the Fed.

That could have significant implications for the tech-heavy Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ), as higher interest rates tend to weigh on growth-stock valuations.

China's hottest trade of 2026 has become its most painful. The STAR 50, Shanghai's index of artificial intelligence and chip companies, has fallen 40% from its July high, according to Reuters reporting. Per the same report, the collapse erased about $480 billion in market value over roughly four months.

Shutterstock

That figure is a paper decline across the whole index. Actual losses depended on when investors bought. Investors who bought before the summer run-up may still be ahead. Investors who bought in July and August took most of the damage.

Dong Baozhen, a Beijing-based fund manager, gave Reuters a blunt verdict: "The stock market later evolved into a speculative crazy bull. And now we see the bubble bursting." Beijing appears to have seen trouble coming. Reuters re[prts state-backed investors sold into rallies during the run-up, a sign policymakers wanted to cool the boom.

China's AI Champions Took the Hardest Hits

The victims read like a list of China's AI champions, per Trending Topics citing Reuters. Humanoid robot maker Unitree has lost about half its value since its August debut. GPU developers MetaX and Moore Threads, seen as China's answer to NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), have roughly halved since July. Optical module suppliers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink trade about 60% below their summer highs. Memory chip maker CXMT fell more than 25% in the month before Oct. 27.

Apple (AAPL) posted a -0.11 correlation with the Nasdaq-100, the first negative reading on record, down from 0.91 in 2025.

Between October 6 and October 23, QQQ (QQQ) dropped 7% while Apple gained 4%, reinforcing its role as a hedge within the tech index.

Apple trades at 45 times earnings near its 52-week high, leaving little margin for a weak quarterly report or worsening memory cost pressures.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Apple didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat AAPL. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

For four decades, Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) and the Nasdaq-100 mostly moved together. As reported on October 26, 2026, Apple's trailing three-month correlation with the index has fallen to about -0.1, per traders at Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS). That is the first negative reading on record, down from 0.91 in 2025.

24/7 Wall St.

Correlation measures how closely two assets move. A reading of one means they move in tandem, zero means there is no relationship, and a negative number means they tend to move in opposite directions. Our calculation uses 63 trading days of daily returns and puts the figure at -0.11 at the October 27 close, against both the index and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ).

A reading like that stands out for a company that held about a 7.5% index weighting as of September. On October 27, both rose: Apple gained 0.93% to $347.10, and QQQ gained 1.27% to $721.25. The break shows up over weeks of trading, so a single day won't reveal it.

Record-Low Correlation Has Held Since August

In data going back to October 1985, the measure never fell below zero before August 2026. Its lowest earlier reading was +0.10 on October 18, 1996, and its peak was 0.97 on June 1, 2020 (our calculation).

DC Studio / Shutterstock.com

Goldman Sachs just gave her a reason to check. On the firm's The Markets podcast, recorded Oct. 22 and posted Oct. 23, Rich Privorotsky, head of European Equities Trading in Goldman's FICC and Equities division, said investors were de-risking out of a crowded trade in AI, semiconductor and hyperscaler stocks. He cited rising capital costs, power constraints and more competition. He also said the prior week saw the largest tech selling ever recorded in Goldman's prime brokerage book.

Pascal Le Segretain / Getty Images

Large-cap tech is stronger, though by a much smaller margin. The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 1.2%, leaving Tesla stock running far ahead of the mega-cap pack.

Autonomous and electric vehicle names are running hotter than broad tech. Within that corner, the Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF (NASDAQ:DRIV) is up 2%, leaving Tesla shares comfortably in front.

ARK Doubles Down on Tesla's Robotaxi Future

ARK Invest's Tasha Keeney repeated the firm's base-case price target of $4,400 per Tesla share by 2031. That call arrived after the prior session's close and puts autonomy at the heart of ARK's long-range case for the company. Most of Tesla's enterprise value in that target year comes from robotaxis in ARK's model, supported by rising adoption of Full Self-Driving among Tesla's North American deliveries.

Exchange-Traded Funds Higher, Equity Futures Mixed Pre-Bell Tuesday as Investors Assess Corporate Earnings

The broad market exchange-traded fund SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) was up 0.4% and the actively traded Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) was 0.6% higher in Tuesday's premarket activity as investors assess results from major technology companies while oil prices eased.

US stock futures were mixed, with S&P 500 Index futures down 0.1%, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures gaining 0.02%, and Nasdaq futures slipping 0.1% before the start of regular trading.

New orders for US durable goods rose by 1.8% in September following a gain of 0.1%, slightly below expectations for a 1.9% increase in a survey compiled by Bloomberg.

The Case-Shiller National Home Price index fell by 0.2% in August before seasonal adjustment following a 0.1% increase in July.

National home prices were up 2.1% year over year, up from 1.9% in July.

The consumer confidence report and the Richmond Fed manufacturing index, both for October, are due at 10 am ET, along with last month's new home sales report.

In premarket activity, bitcoin was down by 0.2%. Among cryptocurrency ETFs, the cryptocurrency fund ProShares Bitcoin Strategy ETF (BITO) was 0.2% lower, Ether ETF (EETH) retreated 0.04%, and Bitcoin & Ether Market Cap Weight ETF (BETH) was 0.4% lower.

Power Play:

Technology

The State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) advanced 0.5%, the iShares US Technology ETF (IYW) was 0.2% higher, and the iShares Expanded Tech Sector ETF (IGM) was down 0.03%. Among semiconductor ETFs, the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) was 1% higher, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) rose by 1.6%.

Celestica (CLS) shares were up more than 12% in premarket activity after the company reported higher Q3 non-GAAP net income and revenue.

Winners and Losers:

Consumer

The State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLP) was down 0.2%, the Vanguard Consumer Staples Index Fund ETF Shares (VDC) was inactive, and the iShares US Consumer Staples ETF (IYK) was up 0.5%. The State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY) gained 0.3%. The VanEck Retail ETF (RTH) was inactive, while the State Street SPDR S&P Retail ETF (XRT) was 0.1% higher.

Whirlpool (WHR) shares were down 5% after the company said it now expects to report a loss for 2026, compared with previous projections for a profit.

Financial

The State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) advanced 0.5%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X Shares (FAS) was up 1.2%, while its bearish counterpart, Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X Shares (FAZ), was 1.1% lower.

S&P Global (SPGI) shares were up 3% in early-hours activity after the company reported higher Q3 adjusted earnings and revenue.

Energy

The iShares US Energy ETF (IYE) was inactive, while the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE) was down by 0.4%.

Energy Fuels (UUUU) stock was up more than 2% before market open after the company said late Monday that it received conditional approval for up to 180 million Australian dollars ($126.4 million) in commitments to support construction of phase 1 of the Donald rare earth and mineral sands Project in Victoria, Australia.

Healthcare

The State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) advanced 0.01%, the Vanguard Health Care Index Fund (VHT) was down 0.1%, while the iShares US Healthcare ETF (IYH) slipped 0.3%. The iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB) was 0.3% lower.

HCA Healthcare (HCA) stock was up more than 1% premarket after the company reported higher Q3 adjusted earnings and revenue.

Industrial

The State Street Industrial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLI) advanced 0.5%, the Vanguard Industrials Index Fund (VIS) gained 1.1%, and the iShares US Industrials ETF (IYJ) was inactive.

SpaceX (SPCX) stock was up more than 1% before the opening bell. Deutsche Bank raised the company's price target to $250 from $235.

Commodities

Front-month US West Texas Intermediate crude oil retreated 0.7% to $101.10 per barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange. Natural gas was up 1.7% at $2.65 per 1 million British Thermal Units. The United States Oil Fund (USO) decreased by 0.7%, while the United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was 0.2% lower.

Gold futures for November lost 0.2% to reach $4,029.00 an ounce on the Comex. Silver futures retreated 1.7% to $53.40 an ounce. SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) was up 0.1%, and the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was 0.9% lower.
